purpose: Define a versioned, product- and domain-neutral, fail-closed evidence intake for separately governed qualified review of a proposed data-protection impact assessment (DPIA). It records scope-bound assessment, risk, mitigation, residual-risk, approval, review, and prior-consultation-trigger evidence references only. It cannot determine whether a DPIA is required, determine high risk or residual risk, approve a DPIA, conclude whether prior consultation is required, establish trusted scope, grant authority, authorize processing, decide release, or enable runtime behavior.

authoritative_external_reference.review_reference: Article 35 and Article 36; any DPIA requirement, risk, residual-risk, approval, prior-consultation, or legal conclusion requires qualified deployment-specific review.

verified_facts: Neural Brain is product- and domain-neutral and has no accepted scoped customer or domain integration.

The current repository does not establish a concrete controller, processing activity, intended purpose, data-subject population, jurisdiction, risk, mitigation, approval, review, or prior-consultation fact.
The repository's protected Memory Core is an internal subsystem and cannot narrow the complete cognitive-system product boundary established by ADR-018.
unknown_facts_not_inferred: whether GDPR, Article 35, or Article 36 applies to a concrete deployment or processing activity
whether a concrete processing activity is likely to result in high risk or has unresolved high residual risk
whether a DPIA is required, complete, approved, current, sufficient, or legally compliant
whether a mitigation is appropriate, implemented, effective, or adequate
whether prior consultation is required or whether a concrete system may process personal data, be deployed, released, or operated

dpia_evidence_intake_template.assessment_unit: One immutable artifact version or digest, concrete proposed deployment and processing activity, immutable authenticated Tenant, Area, and Project scope references, intended-purpose contract version, activity/purpose reference, and jurisdiction evidence combination.
scope_binding_requirements: Tenant, Area, and Project references must identify immutable authenticated runtime-scope evidence. An intake identifier, purpose label, activity label, jurisdiction label, request payload, prompt, observation, model response, memory content, or tool output cannot establish, broaden, or substitute trusted scope.

Artifact, purpose, activity, deployment, and jurisdiction references must name immutable versioned evidence. A DPIA intake is valid only for its exact artifact, authenticated scope, purpose, activity, deployment, and jurisdiction combination; evidence may not be reused across Tenant, Area, Project, artifact, purpose, activity, deployment, or jurisdiction changes without a separate intake and qualified review.

The intake contains durable evidence references and categories only. It must not contain raw personal data, special-category values, criminal-offence data, personal identifiers, credentials, secrets, prompts, memory payloads, consent text, contracts, legal advice, risk narratives containing personal data, or unverified external assertions.

Assessment, risk, mitigation, residual-risk, approval, review, and prior-consultation-trigger entries must state provenance, date, currency, scope, qualified-review treatment, and contradiction status. Unknown, stale, contradictory, unauthenticated, unqualified, or unresolved facts remain explicit deployment-specific release blockers rather than inferred favorable facts.
deterministic_review_order: Verify every required field, exact immutable artifact, authenticated scope, purpose, activity, deployment, jurisdiction, accountable owner, qualified independent reviewer, review date, evidence reference, blocker, and reassessment trigger; any absent, unknown, stale, contradictory, non-immutable, or scope-mismatched fact is incomplete.

Verify linked GDPR applicability, RoPA, personal-data-flow, and reassessment evidence for the same artifact, authenticated scope, purpose, activity, deployment, and jurisdiction; a missing or conflicting prerequisite remains a release blocker.

Record DPIA assessment-method, scope, necessity, proportionality, risk-scenario, likelihood, impact, and risk-register evidence without determining whether a DPIA is required or whether any risk is high; unknown or disputed evidence remains a release blocker.

Record mitigation, control, owner, due-date, effectiveness, residual-risk, approval, and review evidence for qualified review only, without determining adequacy, effectiveness, residual risk, approval validity, or a processing outcome; no favorable later fact compensates for an unresolved earlier fact.

Record the Article 36 prior-consultation-trigger disposition and its qualified evidence without determining whether prior consultation is legally required. An unresolved high-residual-risk evidence item, missing disposition, or missing qualified review remains a release blocker.

Record explicit non-applicability, unknown, conflict, gap, expiry, blocker, reassessment trigger, next review date, and independent release-decision reference. A completed intake remains evidence input only and cannot create a legal, authority, processing, deployment, release, or runtime outcome.

authority_boundary.template_is: a versioned governance and traceability evidence intake for separately governed qualified privacy review
template_is_not: a legal opinion, data-protection impact assessment determination, prior-consultation determination, or compliance certification
a determination that a DPIA is required, a risk is high, residual risk is acceptable, a mitigation is effective, an approval is valid, or prior consultation is legally required
an authenticated Tenant, Area, Project, Session, principal, role, authority, policy, or approval context
a policy decision, Security Floor override, protected-state transition request, or gate decision
a processing, deployment, productive-use, or release approval
a runtime capability enablement or external-effect authorization
an implementation, maturity, recognition, safety, product capability, or production-autonomy claim
authority_boundary.release_boundary: Only separately applicable qualified review, accepted governance, and all Protected Control Plane, transition-gate, evaluation, recognition, and release evidence requirements may decide a concrete processing activity or deployment. This intake never activates a runtime path.

current_blocker.unblock_condition: A concrete proposed deployment supplies every required field, exact immutable artifact and authenticated scope/purpose/activity/jurisdiction evidence, linked prerequisite evidence, accountable owner, qualified independent reviewer, assessment/risk/mitigation/residual-risk/approval/review/prior-consultation-trigger evidence, explicit unknown dispositions, reassessment triggers, and separately governed release evidence.
current_blocker.next_step: Create one immutable DPIA evidence intake per proposed artifact, authenticated Tenant/Area/Project scope, purpose, processing activity, deployment, and jurisdiction combination before any processing-specific or deployment-specific release decision.
